subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Listening and chart completion; choosing past forms / Reported speech with the past perfect; Activate Your English
outcomes: Listen to students talk about their first weeks and complete a chart
Use the past perfect in reported speech
Talk about regrets with I wish and If only

tf.s: Sara had expected a huge number of students.
tf.why: Yes, she expected many students and teachers of many nationalities.

tf.s: 'I'd expected the campus to be large' uses the past perfect.
tf.why: Correct, I'd expected = I had expected.

tf.s: B had not expected such a long way between the buildings.
Zaher's favourite activity is swimming in the sea.
tf.why: Zaher's favourite is volleyball and the gym.

tf.s: 'I forgot my keys,' he said. → He said he had forgotten his keys.
tf.why: Yes, the past simple moves back to the past perfect.

tf.s: In reported speech, verbs move back a tense because the reporting verb is in the present.
tf.why: They move back because the reporting verb is in the past.

tf.s: The past perfect is used for the earlier of two past events.
tf.why: Correct, it shows what happened first.

tf.s: We should use the past perfect for every past action.
tf.why: It is only for the earlier of two past events.

tf.s: 'I wish I had studied more' is a regret about the past.
tf.why: Yes, wish + past perfect shows a past regret.

tf.s: 'If only I hadn't wasted my time' means I am happy I wasted my time.
tf.why: It shows regret: I wish I had not wasted it.

boxes.q: Report: 'I forgot my keys,' he said.
o: He said he had forgotten his keys.
He said he forgets his keys.
He said he has forgot his keys.

boxes.q: Report: 'We didn't see him,' she said.
o: She said they had not seen him.
She said they don't see him.
She said they not saw him.

boxes.why: She expected a very big university.
Zaher enjoys volleyball and the gym.

boxes.q: Which is the past perfect of 'swim'?
boxes.why: The past participle of swim is swum.

boxes.q: Which is the past perfect of 'catch'?
Which sentence shows a past regret?
o: I wish I had studied more.

boxes.q: Why do verbs move back in reported speech?
o: the reporting verb is in the past
boxes.why: Said/told in the past cause backshift.

boxes.q: How is the past perfect formed?

mcq.q: When do we use the past perfect?
o: for the earlier of two past events
mcq.why: It shows which past action came first.

mcq.q: Which verb in this sentence is in the past perfect: 'She had borrowed a book before class'?
What did Sara expect besides many students?
mcq.why: She expected teachers from many nationalities.

mcq.q: Which phrase do we use with the past perfect to express regret?
mcq.why: I wish + past perfect expresses regret.

mcq.q: Report: 'I have never seen the sea,' he said.
o: He said he had never seen the sea.
He said he has never seen the sea.
He said he never sees the sea.
He said he had never saw the sea.

mcq.q: You didn't revise and failed. Which sentence shows regret?

o: Before I came here I had never used a library.
Before I came here I have never use a library.
Before I had came here I never used a library.
Before I come here I had never used a library.
mcq.why: The earlier event uses the past perfect.

mcq.q: Why is 'realised' used and not 'had realised' in 'When I arrived, I realised I was late'?
o: both happened at the same time, so the past perfect is not needed
mcq.why: The past perfect is only for an earlier event.

mcq.q: What is the difference between 'I wish I studied' and 'I wish I had studied'?
o: 'had studied' is a regret about the past
mcq.why: Wish + past perfect looks back at the past.

mcq.q: 'She told me she had visited the library.' What does the past perfect show?
o: the visit happened before she told me
mcq.why: The visit came first, before the telling.
